lessons.title: The Earliest Cities and Harappa
lessons.summary: Discovering Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, planned drainage, the Great Bath, and Bronze Age trade.

sections.heading: Discovery of the Indus Cities
sections.passage: Nearly 4,700 years ago, some of the earliest planned cities in the Indian subcontinent developed along the Indus River valley. The first city excavated by archaeologists in the 1920s was Harappa in Punjab (now in Pakistan), followed by Mohenjo-Daro in Sindh. Because Harappa was found first, this ancient urban culture is known as the Harappan or Indus Valley Civilisation.

sections.heading: Town Planning and the Great Bath
sections.passage: Harappan cities were divided into two main parts: a higher west part called the Citadel, and a larger lower town in the east where common citizens lived. Buildings were constructed using durable, interlocking baked bricks. In Mohenjo-Daro, a special tank called the Great Bath was built lined with bricks, coated with plaster, and sealed watertight with a layer of natural tar (bitumen), likely used for ritual bathing.

sections.heading: Drainage, Crafts, and Seals
sections.passage: Harappan cities featured remarkably advanced sanitary systems. Drains along streets were laid in straight lines, covered with inspection stone slabs, and connected to household toilets and bathing areas. Harappan artisans made pottery with black designs, terracotta toys, beads from carnelian stones, copper tools, and rectangular soapstone seals carved with animal figures and undeciphered script.

questions.prompt: Which was the first excavated city of the Indus Valley Civilisation?
questions.explanation: Harappa was the first ancient city excavated in this civilization, giving it the name Harappan Civilisation.

questions.prompt: In Mohenjo-Daro, the Great Bath was made watertight using:
questions.explanation: Baked bricks were plastered and sealed with natural tar (bitumen) to prevent water leakage.

questions.prompt: The elevated western part of a Harappan city is called the:
questions.explanation: The citadel was the higher, fortified western section holding public buildings and storehouses.

questions.prompt: What material was used to make rectangular Harappan seals?
questions.explanation: Harappan seals were intricately carved from soft soapstone (steatite) and pressed onto clay goods.

lessons.title: Nouns, Verbs, and Adjectives
lessons.summary: Building clear English sentences using naming words, action words, and describing words.

sections.heading: Nouns: Naming Words
sections.passage: A noun is a word that names a person, place, animal, thing, or concept. Common nouns name general items (e.g., river, student, tree, village), whereas proper nouns name specific entities and always begin with a capital letter (e.g., Ganga, Priya, Delhi, India). Abstract nouns name feelings and ideas that cannot be touched (e.g., courage, honesty, kindness).

sections.heading: Verbs: Action Words and Helping Verbs
sections.passage: A verb expresses an action, state, or occurrence in a sentence. Action verbs show what someone does (e.g., runs, sings, writes, reads). Helping verbs (auxiliary verbs) assist main verbs to indicate tense, certainty, or time (e.g., is, are, was, were, has, have, will). Every complete English sentence must have at least one verb.

sections.heading: Adjectives: Describing Words
sections.passage: An adjective modifies or describes a noun or pronoun by giving details about its size, colour, number, quality, or condition. In the phrase 'three ripe yellow mangoes', the words 'three', 'ripe', and 'yellow' are all adjectives describing the noun 'mangoes'. Adjectives make written and spoken communication precise and vivid.

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'The brave girl climbed the tall tree', which word is a verb?
questions.explanation: 'Climbed' is an action verb describing what the girl did.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a proper noun?
questions.explanation: 'Himalayas' is the specific name of a mountain range and begins with a capital letter.

questions.prompt: Identify the adjective in: 'She drank cold milk.'
questions.explanation: 'Cold' describes the condition and temperature of the noun 'milk'.

questions.prompt: Words that describe feelings or ideas like 'kindness' and 'honesty' are:
questions.explanation: Abstract nouns represent intangible qualities, concepts, or emotions.
